transcript.text: Warren Buffett and one of his friends
graduated from Columbia the same year.
He said that guy was smarter and worked
harder than him. But then Warren ends up
getting into investing with Ben Graham,
who's a huge investor at the time, and
his friend went into the steel business
when American steel was booming. So,
fast forward 30, 40, 50 years, his
friend did well, but not even close to
what Warren did. And the lesson that
Warren learned was that it wasn't about
how hard you row, it's about the boat
you're in. And I love that because it
demonstrates the concept behind
leverage, which is getting more for what
you put in. So, Warren got more for his
effort compared to his buddy who smarter
and harder working by his own
suggestion. And so, over my career, I
make more now than I did before because
I understand the four levels of
leverage. Number one is collaboration,
so hiring other people to work for you.
Number two is capital, using other
people's money. Number three is code or
technology. If I can build a software
once and then millions of people can use
it, that same software has no additional
work to provide value. And then fourth,
you've got content. You can make a video
once and then millions of people can
watch it. Follow along if you want to
learn from some of the mistakes I made
in growing my business.
